title: Day 700 — Sheinbaum Delivers Second Government Report From National Palace, Cites 51% Homicide Drop and Sovereignty Message
detail: On September 1, 2026 (Day 700, Tuesday), President Claudia Sheinbaum delivered her Second Government Report ("En Defensa de la Soberanía"-style annual address) from the National Palace at 11:00 AM CDMX time, replacing that day's regular mañanera. Headline claims: intentional homicides down 51% since the administration's October 2024 start (about 44 fewer deaths per day) and high-impact crimes down 32%; the monthly minimum wage risen from 2,800 pesos (2018) to 9,584 pesos, with labor poverty at its lowest level since 2005; annual inflation at 3.12% (July 2026) on a downward trend; the peso trading near 17/USD; roughly 60 million people employed and unemployment at 2.7%; H1 2026 foreign direct investment of approximately $34.97 billion (+2.1% YoY); GDP growth revised to 1.4% QoQ / 1.9% YoY for Q2 2026; and a new welfare push toward 42.86 million beneficiaries by year-end backed by roughly 1 trillion pesos in social spending. On security, the government cited 63,000 people detained for crimes since October 2024, 207 priority targets arrested, 32,824 firearms seized, 519 tonnes of drugs seized and 2,725 clandestine labs dismantled. Health and infrastructure figures included 33 new hospitals, 23+ million "Salud Casa por Casa" home visits, Tren Maya ridership of 2.5 million passengers, and a Pemex financial-debt reduction of roughly $20 billion. Sheinbaum highlighted a new indigenous-rights law and framed welfare programs as "turning love into public policy." She struck a conciliatory, unity-focused tone toward Morena ahead of the 2027 midterms — "que nadie se equivoque: aquí no hay divisiones, aquí no hay rompimientos" — while repeating her sovereignty line that international cooperation "no significa sumisión" and that Mexico's sovereignty "no se negocia, no se entrega y no se comparte." Opposition reaction was sharp: PAN deputy Federico Döring presented a rival "informe real" citing low growth, rising debt, Pemex's financial crisis, insecurity and disappearances; PAN also noted her administration's 0.8% average growth trails AMLO's 1.1%. PRI national leader Alejandro Moreno accused Morena of degrading quality of life and shielding drug traffickers.
